classificationPolicy.principle: Allowlist only: a rule governs a dimension only when its text fixes that builtin (or the explicitly named family containing it) and that question. Loose keyword similarity and requirements for a future contract do not count.
classificationPolicy.enumerationCriterion: A governed dimension is DECIDED-AND-ENUMERATED only when the banked coverage artifact marks it covered across every inventory profile; otherwise it is DECIDED-NOT-ENUMERATED.
classificationPolicy.uncertaintyRule: If the decided text does not fix the builtin/question pair, classify it UNDECIDED.

mappingRules.family: checked Int and mixed numeric arithmetic
mappingRules.rationale: The rule names these operations, their evaluation and failure order, and closes strictness, purity, representation, and identity for numeric primitives.
The rule fixes ordered-predicate NaN results and the numeric-primitive closure fixes the remaining five questions.

mappingRules.family: explicit numeric conversions and bit codecs
mappingRules.rationale: Float/Int conversion and canonical Float-bit behavior are fixed explicitly; the numeric-primitive closure supplies strictness, order, purity, and identity.
The accepted grammar, complete consumption, range result, and absence result are fixed, with the numeric-primitive closure governing the other questions.

mappingRules.family: semantic equality, identity, and hashing operations
mappingRules.rationale: The rule defines domains, results, rejections, evaluation order, purity, observable identity, representation independence, and allocation behavior.
NaN and other unhashable values have the named BEAGLE-UNHASHABLE-VALUE admission failure for Map/Set uses of these operations.
The constructor's decomposition, value identity, representation, canonical form, Unicode failure, purity, and lack of observable allocation identity are explicit.
Generated symbols have explicit origin/ordinal identity, left-to-right FreshName effects, tagged representation, and eager inputs; no gensym failure is decided.
The rule fixes the returned textual parts and Symbol comparison, but does not claim unrelated operational questions for these broadly typed builtins.
The truth table, operand identity, short-circuit order, purity, allocation-free implementation, strictness boundary, and foreign-value failure are explicit.
The rule names these traversals, fixes their order independent of representation, and states that consumed elements are strict.
Each callback completes before the next begins in the declared traversal order.

mappingRules.family: Map/Set insertion, replacement, and deletion operations
mappingRules.rationale: The rule fixes insertion positions, replacement/deletion/reinsertion order, persistent-update representation independence, and strict consumption.
List/Vec authored order and Map/Set left-to-right insertion order are fixed, strict, and independent of the host collection representation.
Stable results, strict consumption, representation independence, and the named total-order/effectful-comparator rejections are explicit.
Promotion has explicit deep-copy representation and identity, eager left-to-right allocation effects, strictness, and named promotion/escape failures.
Within macro evaluation, bodies and sequential bindings are eager and left-to-right, the phase is pure, and allocation is confined to compile-time syntax and values.

mappingRules.family: entropy, UUID, shuffle, time, and concurrency operations
mappingRules.rationale: These named nondeterministic families require explicit capabilities/providers and use the document-wide eager, left-to-right rule. The rule only requires future failure/result/ownership contracts, so those questions remain UNDECIDED here.
